title: Human Body Systems Overview
summary: This lesson surveys the major organ systems of the human body and explains their primary functions. Understanding how these systems work together provides a foundation for health and disease concepts.

sections.heading: The Skeletal and Muscular Systems
sections.body:
The skeletal system is made of bones, cartilage, and joints. It provides support, protects vital organs, and stores minerals like calcium. The muscular system works with the skeleton to produce movement through contraction of muscle fibers.

Muscles are classified as skeletal (voluntary), cardiac (involuntary, heart), and smooth (involuntary, walls of organs). Together, bones and muscles allow us to stand, walk, and perform fine motor tasks.

sections.heading: The Circulatory and Respiratory Systems
sections.body:
The circulatory system consists of the heart, blood vessels, and blood. Its main job is to transport oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products throughout the body.

The respiratory system includes the nose, trachea, lungs, and diaphragm. It brings in oxygen and removes carbon dioxide, which the circulatory system then delivers to cells for energy production.

sections.heading: The Digestive, Excretory, and Endocrine Systems
sections.body:
The digestive system breaks down food into nutrients that can be absorbed into the bloodstream. Major organs include the mouth, stomach, intestines, liver, and pancreas.

The excretory (urinary) system removes waste and maintains water balance using the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra. The endocrine system releases hormones from glands such as the pituitary, thyroid, and adrenal glands to regulate growth, metabolism, and stress responses.

sections.heading: The Nervous and Immune Systems
sections.body:
The nervous system, composed of the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves, processes sensory information and coordinates actions. It enables rapid communication via electrical signals.

The immune system defends the body against pathogens using white blood cells, antibodies, and organs like the spleen and lymph nodes. It works closely with other systems to keep the body healthy.

key_terms.meaning: A group of organs that work together to perform a major function.
The maintenance of stable internal conditions despite external changes.
A chemical messenger released by glands that travels through the bloodstream to target cells.
A nerve cell that transmits electrical signals in the nervous system.
The process by which kidneys remove waste and excess substances from the blood.
Rhythmic muscle contractions that move food through the digestive tract.

quiz.q: Which system is primarily responsible for transporting oxygen to body cells?
quiz.why: The circulatory system carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to tissues.

quiz.q: What is the main function of the skeletal system?
quiz.why: Bones give the body shape, protect organs, and serve as attachment points for muscles.

quiz.q: Which organ is part of both the digestive and endocrine systems?
quiz.why: The pancreas secretes digestive enzymes and hormones like insulin.
Homeostasis keeps variables such as temperature and pH within narrow limits.

flashcards.front: What does the respiratory system do?
flashcards.back: It exchanges gases: takes in oxygen and removes carbon dioxide.

flashcards.front: Name the two main types of muscle tissue.
flashcards.back: Skeletal (voluntary) and cardiac (involuntary); smooth muscle is a third type found in organs.
Wave-like muscle contractions that move food through the digestive tract.

flashcards.front: Where are hormones released into the bloodstream?
flashcards.back: From endocrine glands such as the pituitary, thyroid, and adrenal glands.
